newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel stable against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel stable against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed almost unchanged against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Wednesday in lacklustre trading, dealers said.

"Trading was very quiet today and volume was relatively low. The shekel was traded in a tight range. The basket was also stable and the Bank of Israel was not seen in the market," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket rate, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for more than a month.
"The local market is waiting to see what the reaction will be to Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before the U.S. Congress (later) on Wednesday," the dealer said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3380 shekels against 3.3390 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6418 shekels against 3.6411 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7590 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7412 on Tuesday and against the mark at 1.9947 shekels against 1.9939 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3380 shekels.
